matches.title: Sunderland vs Manchester United
matches.description: Watch Sunderland vs Manchester United highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 9, 2026. The spotlight of the Premier League fell upon the Stadium of Light on May 9, 2026 , as two sides engaged in a grueling tactical battle. With an attendance of 47,233 fans, the atmosphere was set for a high-stakes encounter that would be decided by the narrowest of margins. Early VAR Tension and Tactical Chess The opening exchanges saw both teams struggle to find a rhythm in the final third. The first major talking point occurred in the 19th minute when the referee paused play for a lengthy VAR check regarding a potential penalty for Sunderland . Ultimately, no spot-kick was awarded, and the game continued its cagey pattern. Enzo Le Fee and Amad were frequent deliverers from corner situations, but their service failed to connect with teammates in the box, leaving both defenses largely untroubled throughout a goalless first half. Disciplined Defending and Midfield Friction As the second half unfolded, the physical nature of the contest intensified, leading to a flurry of bookings for the visitors. Mason Mount was shown a yellow card for a previous foul, followed shortly by Joshua Zirkzee , who was booked for pulling an opponent's shirt. Both managers turned to their benches to break the deadlock; Manchester United introduced Patrick Dorgu and Bryan Mbeumo , while Sunderland brought on Nilson Angulo to inject pace. Despite these changes, the quality of delivery from set-pieces remained low, with Bruno Fernandes seeing several corners fail to reach their intended targets. Late Goalkeeping Heroics and Penalty Drama The match reached a boiling point during five minutes of stoppage time. Matheus Cunha forced a spectacular save from Robin Roefs in the 93rd minute, nearly snatching a late winner for the visitors. However, the game’s most controversial moment followed immediately after, as Matheus Cunha went down in the box under pressure. The referee deemed it a dive, booking the forward and dismissing the penalty appeals. A final blocked shot from Bryan Mbeumo and a series of clearances from Harry Maguire ensured the match ended in a stalemate, with possession split almost evenly between the two clubs.

matches.title: Wolverhampton vs Sunderland
matches.description: Watch Wolverhampton vs Sunderland highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 2, 2026. Molineux played host to a high-stakes Premier League encounter as Wolverhampton and Sunderland faced off in a match defined by tactical discipline and sudden shifts in momentum. The atmosphere was electric on May 2, 2026 , as both sides looked to seize control of a contest that promised drama from the opening whistle. Early Breakthrough and Defensive Discipline The visitors found their rhythm early in the match, making their intentions clear through set-piece efficiency. In the 17th minute, Sunderland silenced the home crowd when Granit Xhaka delivered a pinpoint corner from the right flank. Nordi Mukiele rose highest in the box, connecting with a powerful header that flew past the goalkeeper to give the Black Cats an early lead. The goal rewarded the visitors' clinical start, but the game took a drastic turn just seven minutes later. In the 24th minute, the match official was forced to reach for his back pocket following a serious foul by Daniel Ballard . The referee showed no hesitation in brandishing a straight red card, dismissing the defender and leaving Sunderland to play more than an hour of football with only ten men. Despite the numerical disadvantage, the visitors retreated into a compact defensive shape, with goalkeeper Robin Roefs proving a formidable barrier. Tolu Arokodare spearheaded the Wolverhampton response, seeing several headed efforts saved by Roefs as the first half drew to a close with the scoreline still favoring the away side. The Bueno Connection and VAR Tension Wolverhampton returned for the second half with renewed vigor, immediately pinning the ten-man visitors back into their own territory. The pressure finally told in the 54th minute through a moment of familial-named synchronicity. Hugo Bueno swung a high-quality corner into the danger zone, where Santiago Bueno was waiting to meet it. The defender’s header found the back of the net, but the celebrations were momentarily halted as the referee initiated a VAR check. After a tense review, the goal was confirmed, drawing the hosts level and leaving Granit Xhaka so incensed he received a yellow card for dissent. Seeking a winner, the Wolverhampton bench introduced Rodrigo Gomes and Angel Gomes to inject more creativity into the final third. The hosts dominated the ball, maintaining 58% possession throughout the contest, but they found it increasingly difficult to break through a resilient Sunderland block. Adam Armstrong saw an effort ruled out for offside, while Arokodare continued to test the defense, only to see his best efforts blocked by the determined backline. A Frantic Finish at Molineux As the clock ticked toward the 90th minute, the tension among the 29,632 fans in attendance reached a fever pitch. Sunderland ’s defensive effort became increasingly desperate, leading to a flurry of bookings as Dennis Cirkin and Robin Roefs both entered the referee's book for fouls and dissent respectively. Despite the pressure, the visitors nearly snatched a late winner against the run of play in stoppage time when Nordi Mukiele forced a sharp save from the Wolves keeper following a cross from Trai Hume . In the final moments, Wolverhampton threw everything forward, with Tolu Arokodare sending a late effort wide of the target after being set up by Adam Armstrong . However, the ten men of Sunderland held firm through three minutes of added time, securing a gritty point on the road. The final whistle brought an end to a pulsating encounter where both sides could take pride in their resilience, even if the winning goal remained elusive.

matches.title: Sunderland vs Chelsea FC
matches.description: Watch Sunderland vs Chelsea highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 24, 2026. The atmosphere at the Stadium of Light was electric for this high-stakes Premier League encounter on May 24, 2026 . Both teams took to the pitch with clear tactical intent, knowing that every point is vital in the closing stages of the top-flight campaign. Hume Strikes Early for the Hosts Sunderland established their dominance early in the match, utilizing the set-piece delivery of Granit Xhaka to test the visitors' resolve. The breakthrough arrived in the 25th minute following a moment of technical brilliance. A sequence involving Robin Roefs and Luke O'Nien set the stage for Trai Hume , who unleashed a clinical right-footed volley into the back of the net. The goal gave the home side a deserved lead and left Chelsea searching for answers as they struggled to break through a resilient defensive line before the interval. Drama and a Turning Point After the Break The second half began in chaotic fashion for the Londoners. In the 50th minute, disaster struck for the visitors when Malo Gusto inadvertently turned the ball into his own net, doubling Sunderland 's advantage. Chelsea responded swiftly to the setback, as Cole Palmer clinical finish from outside the box pulled a goal back in the 56th minute following an assist from Pedro Neto . However, the momentum shifted back to the hosts just six minutes later when Wesley Fofana received a second yellow card and was sent off, leaving the visitors to fight the remainder of the contest with ten men. Resilient Defense Secures the Win As the clock ticked down, the match became increasingly physical, with the referee issuing several cautions to maintain control. Players including Enzo Fernandez , Granit Xhaka , and Habib Diarra all saw yellow as tensions flared. Despite tactical substitutions from both managers, including the introduction of Liam Delap for Chelsea and Chris Rigg for Sunderland , the scoreline remained unchanged. Robert Sanchez made a few late claims to keep his side in the hunt, but Sunderland held firm to secure a 2-1 victory, navigating through 14 minutes of stoppage time to claim all three points.
